--- BUILDING.md ---
1| Building Ambassador
2| ===================
3| 
4| If you just want to **use** Ambassador, check out https://www.getambassador.io/! You don't need to build anything, and in fact you shouldn't.
5| 
6| TL;DR
7| -----
8| 
9| ```
10| git clone https://github.com/datawire/ambassador
11| cd ambassador
12| # Development should be on branches based on the `master` branch
13| git checkout master
14| git checkout -b username/feature/my-branch-here
15| make DOCKER_REGISTRY=-
16| ```
17| 
18| That will build an Ambassador Docker image for you but not push it anywhere. To actually push the image into a registry so that you can use it for Kubernetes, set `DOCKER_REGISTRY` to a registry that you have permissions to push to.
19| 
20| **It is important to use `make` rather than trying to just do a `docker build`.** Actually assembling a Docker image for Ambassador involves quite a few steps before the image can be built.
21| 
22| Branching
23| ---------
24| 
25| 1. `master` is the branch from which Ambassador releases are cut. There should be no other activity on `master`.
26| 
27| 2. **All development must be on branches cut from `master`.** When you have things working and tested, submit a pull request back to `master`.
28|    - There is a special type of branch for e.g. minor doc changes called `nobuild`. Any branch that matches `^nobuild.*` skips all CI activities for that branch.
29|    
30| 3. Once your branch is at a point where it's ready for review and testing, open a GitHub PR against `master`.
31|    - The PR will trigger CI to perform a build and run tests.
32|    - Tests **must** be passing for the PR to be merged.
33| 
34| 4. When all is well, maintainers will merge the PR into `master`.
35| 
36| 5. Releases are driven by the maintainers applying tags to `master`.
37| 
38| Documentation Changes
39| ---------------------
40| 
41| Note that documentation changes _still follow the PR process_. If you're making minor changes (fixing typos, for example) it's OK to use a `nobuild` branch as above. If you're doing significant changes, you might want to allow CI to run by using a branch name `doc/major-doc-changes` or the like.
42| 
43| Unit Tests
44| ----------
45| 
46| Unit tests for Ambassador live in the `ambassador/tests` directory. Within that directory, you'll find directories with names that start with three digits (`000-default`, `001-broader-v0`, etc); each of these directories describes a test environment. Tests run on every build of Ambassador, and test Ambassador's ability to transform a known Ambassador configuration into a known intermediate configuration and a known Envoy configuration.
47| 
48| **You are strongly encouraged to add tests when you add features.** Adding a new test is simply a matter of adding a new test directory under `ambassador/tests`. Start its name with three digits; the rest of the name should be a brief description of what you're testing, with no spaces.
49| 
50| Call the test directory (e.g. `ambassador/tests/002-tls-module-1`) `$TESTDIR`. Then:
51| 
52| - The test MUST contain an Ambassador configuration.
53|    - For every test except `000-default`, the configuration is the set of YAML files in `$TESTDIR/config`. 
54|       - The `000-default` test is special: it contains the magic `TEST_DEFAULT_CONFIG` marker, which says to use `ambassador/default-config` for configuration.
55|    - Some tests will also need to include other files, e.g. TLS certificates. These should be in `config` as well -- see the `002-tls-module-1` test for an example.
56| 
57| - The test SHOULD contain a known-good Ambassador intermediate configuration dump.
58|    - The intermediate configuration is generated by `ambassador dump`.
59|    - The known good intermediate configuration is in `$TESTDIR/gold.intermediate.json`.
60|    - If `gold.intermediate.json` is present, the test will generate `$TESTDIR/intermediate.json` and compare it with the known good version.
61| 
62| - The test SHOULD contain a known-good Envoy configuration dump.
63|    - The Envoy configuration is generated by `ambassador config`.
64|    - The known good Envoy configuration is in `$TESTDIR/gold.json`.
65|    - If `gold.json` is present:
66|       - The test will generate `$TESTDIR/envoy.json` and compare it with the known good version.
67|       - The test will also hand `$TESTDIR/envoy.json` to Envoy for validation -- this step runs inside Docker, and the test directory is mounted inside the Docker container as `/etc/ambassador-config`.
68| 
69| - In all cases, Ambassador's diagnostic service is invoked on the Ambassador configuration, and the results are checked for internal consistency.
70| 
71| To extend a test, change the configuration in `$TESTDIR/config`, then run a build (`make DOCKER_REGISTRY=-`) which will run all the CI tests. The tests will fail - if not, you didn't really change the test configuration, right? - but they'll output the diffs they found against the known-good versions. If all looks well, you can update the known-good versions:
72| 
73| - `mv $TESTDIR/intermediate.json $TESTDIR/gold.intermediate.json`
74| - `mv $TESTDIR/envoy.json $TESTDIR/gold.json`
75| 
76| and then commit all the changes you made in `$TESTDIR`.
77| 
78| End-to-End Tests
79| ----------------
80| 
81| Ambassador's end-to-end tests are run by CI for pull requests, release candidates, and releases: we will not release an Ambassador for which the end-to-end tests are failing. **Again, you are strongly encouraged to add end-to-end test coverage for features you add.** 
82| 
83| For more information on the end-to-end tests, see [their README](end-to-end/README.md).
84| 
85| Version Numbering
86| -----------------
87| 
88| Version numbers will be determined by Git tags for actual releases. You are free to pick whatever version numbers you like when doing test builds.
89| 
90| Normal Workflow
91| ---------------
92| 
93| 0. `export DOCKER_REGISTRY=$registry`
94| 
95|    This sets the registry to which to push Docker images and is **mandatory**.
96| 
97|    "dwflynn" will push to Dockerhub with user `dwflynn`
98|    "gcr.io/flynn" will push to GCR with user `flynn`
99| 
100|    If you're using Minikube and don't want to push at all, set `DOCKER_REGISTRY` to "-".
101| 
102|    You can separately tweak the registry from which images will be _pulled_ using `AMBASSADOR_REGISTRY` and `STATSD_REGISTRY`. See the files in `templates` for more here.
103| 
104| 1. Use a private branch cut from `master` for your work.
105| 
106| 2. Hack away, then `make`. This will:
107| 
108|    a. Run tests and bail if something doesn't pass.
109|    b. Build Docker images, and push them if DOCKER_REGISTRY says to.
110|    c. Build YAML files for you in `doc/yaml`.
111| 
112|    You can easily `kubectl apply` the updated YAML files and see your changes in your Kubernetes cluster.
113| 
114| 3. Commit to your feature branch.
115| 
116|    Remember: _not to `master`_.
117| 
118| 4. Open a pull request against `master` when you're ready to ship.
119| 
120| What if I Don't Want to Push My Images?
121| ---------------------------------------
122| 
123| **NOTE WELL**: if you're not using Minikube, this is almost certainly a mistake.
124| 
125| But if you are using Minikube, you can set `DOCKER_REGISTRY` to "-" to prevent pushing the images. The Makefile (deliberately) requires you to set DOCKER_REGISTRY, so you can't just unset it.
126| 
127| Building the Documentation and Website
128| --------------------------------------
129| 
130| Use `make website` to build the docs and website. See [the README](docs/README.md) for docs-specific steps. The `docs/build-website.sh` script (used by `make`) follows those steps and then performs some additional hacks for website use.

To resolve the security issues reported, the following changes are required:

### 1. Relocate Configuration Directory
The issue reports that writing to `/etc/ambassador-config` triggers security alerts. We should move this directory to a non-system location.

**Edit `ambassador/Dockerfile`:**
*   Change line 48: `RUN mkdir /etc/ambassador-config` to `RUN mkdir /ambassador-config`.
*   Change line 51: `COPY default-config/ /etc/ambassador-demo-config` to `COPY default-config/ /ambassador-demo-config` (to maintain consistency with the new pattern).

**Note:** This change will require updates to any scripts (like `entrypoint.sh` or `kubewatch.py`) and Kubernetes manifests that expect configuration at `/etc/ambassador-config`.

### 2. Implement Non-Root Execution
The issue suggests that `entrypoint.sh`, `python3`, and `envoy` should run as a non-root user.

**Edit `ambassador/Dockerfile`:**
*   Create a non-root user and group using `RUN addgroup -S ambassador && adduser -S ambassador -G ambassador`.
*   Ensure the `/application` directory and the new `/ambassador-config` directory are owned by this user so the application can write to them if necessary.
*   Change the `ENTRYPOINT` or add a `USER ambassador` instruction. 

**Warning:** Since the current `Dockerfile` performs installations and directory creations as root, the `USER` instruction should be placed after the `pip3 install` and `setup.py install` steps.

### Summary of Change Plan
1.  **`ambassador/Dockerfile`**:
    *   Add user/group creation: `RUN addgroup -S ambassador && adduser -S ambassador -G ambassador`.
    *   Update config paths: Change `/etc/ambassador-config` to `/ambassador-config` and `/etc/ambassador-demo-config` to `/ambassador-demo-config`.
    *   Update permissions: `RUN chown -R ambassador:ambassador /application /ambassador-config /ambassador-demo-config`.
    *   Switch user: Add `USER ambassador` before the `ENTRYPOINT`.
2.  **Post-implementation**:
    *   Verify `entrypoint.sh` and `kubewatch.py` do not rely on absolute paths in `/etc`.
    *   Verify that the application has sufficient permissions in the new `/ambassador-config` location.
